message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value (standard conditions) | Notes |
|----------|-----------------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average) | Weighted average of isotopes H‑1, H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium). |
| **Isotopes** | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) | Deuterium is stable; tritium is radioactive (half‑life ~12.3 yr). |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest of all elements. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Highest among all elements. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | Negative value indicates energy release when an electron is added. |
| **Molecular form** | H₂ (diatomic) | Most common form in nature; covalent bond. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; liquid only under high pressure. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solid only at very low temperatures. |
| **Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | Lightest gas; less dense than air. |
| **Density (liquid, 20 °C)** | 0.0708 g cm⁻³ | Still lighter than most liquids. |
| **Specific heat (gas, 25 °C)** | 14.304 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ | High due to low molar mass. |
| **Molar volume (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | Standard molar volume. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals. | Forms H⁺ (proton) in aqueous solution; key in acid-base chemistry. |
| **Bonding** | Forms single covalent bonds; can form H₂O, H₂S, CH₄, etc. | Can also form hydrogen bonds (e.g., in water). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer series (visible) | Classic example of atomic hydrogen spectrum. |
| **Role in stars** | Fusion fuel (proton–proton chain, CNO cycle) | Hydrogen burning powers the Sun and other stars. |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), metallurgy, semiconductor manufacturing, cryogenics, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents), etc. | Widely used in industry and research. |

### Quick Summary

- **Atomic**: Lightest element, one proton, one electron, high electronegativity and ionization energy.
- **Physical**: Extremely low melting/boiling points, very low density, high specific heat.
- **Chemical**: Forms H₂ gas; highly reactive; key in acid–base chemistry and as a reducing agent.
- **Isotopic**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, used in heavy water), tritium (radioactive, used in nuclear fusion research).
- **Astrophysical**: Primary fuel for stellar fusion; abundant in the universe.

These properties make hydrogen unique among elements and central to many fields—from chemistry and physics to energy technology and astrophysics.
